questions.stem: Per this page, what happens on Java 21 when a virtual thread makes a blocking I/O call inside a synchronized block?

options.text: The I/O call throws an exception, since blocking is not allowed under a lock
options.says: The page's example does its blocking I/O inside the synchronized block; the cost it names is scalability, not an exception.

options.text: The virtual thread unmounts as usual, and only the lock is held for longer
options.says: The page says that while pinned the virtual thread cannot unmount from its carrier.

options.text: The virtual thread stays on its carrier, so that carrier thread is blocked too
options.says: The page says synchronized pins the virtual thread to its carrier, which is blocked along with it during the I/O.

origin.section: 5. Using synchronized instead of ReentrantLock with virtual threads

questions.stem: Per this page, what can happen to writers under a heavy read load with a ReentrantReadWriteLock built with its default settings?

options.text: They may starve, as readers keep taking the read lock before them
options.says: The page says the default non-fair lock can starve writers, because readers keep acquiring the read lock.

options.text: They may jump ahead, as the default lock serves writers before readers
options.says: The page says the default lock is non-fair and that readers keep acquiring the read lock, which is what starves writers.

options.text: They may overlap readers, as the write lock still lets readers in
options.says: The page says a writer needs exclusive access, with no concurrent readers or writers.
